ops.title: Releasing the cc-transcript family — cc-pushback→cc-steer rename; parallel sessions grab version tags (ship the leftover migration as the next patch); migration branches drift under parallel work; uv index CDN lag vs --upgrade-package for fresh publishes; test-deps-in-dev-extra gate quirk; ccxbench pytest/corpus quirks; transient GitHub Pages deploy flakes
ops.body:
Release-process facts for the cc-transcript family (cc-transcript, captain-hook, cc-pushback, cc-sentiment, cc-context/bench), from the v8 rollout (2026-07-03). For the `[tool.uv] environments` macOS/Linux lock scoping (required in every consumer), see [[cc-transcript-v8-downstream-uv-lock]].

**ALWAYS diagnose against `origin/main`, never the local checkout.** In these jj-colocated repos the local working copy sits at a *stale detached HEAD* (jj hasn't synced it), so `git log`/`git grep`/`git describe HEAD` on the local tree routinely show pre-migration code and mismatched tags — this caused false "regression"/"orphaned release/lost work" alarms **twice** (captain-hook, then cc-sentiment: `git describe HEAD`=`v0.2.128-1` while `origin/main` was already at `v0.2.129`=the published migration). Before ever concluding work was lost or a release is orphaned, check `git rev-parse origin/main` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tag> origin/main`. Also expect the local main checkout to hold an *unpushed parallel-session feature commit* diverged from `origin/main` at the last release (e.g. captain-hook local `383cef4c` steering pack 0.4.0 vs my pushed fixes on `origin/main`) — leave it, it rebases; a FF-only push (`<sha>:refs/heads/main`) can't clobber it. Recover genuinely-unmerged fix branches (verify with `git cherry origin/main <branch>`: `+`=unique/unmerged, `-`=already landed) by cherry-picking the *fix commit itself* onto current `origin/main` (the branch's own base may be ancient/pre-v8 — ignore the huge `diff origin/main..branch`, `git show <sha>` is the real change).

**Migration branches drift under parallel work.** The family repos are jj-colocated (detached HEAD; use git only — the user actively pushes to them mid-release). Migration branches get cut, then main advances: during v8, captain-hook's `cc-transcript-v8` branch ended up +6/−37 vs main (main had cut 2 releases meanwhile); cc-sentiment's was only 2 behind. Redo = REBASE the preserved branch onto current main, don't redo from scratch — the work survives on `refs/heads/*` + `refs/jj/keep/*` (verify with `git for-each-ref --contains <sha>`). mergiraf auto-resolves most conflicts; a v8 export-list conflict (feature added exports, migration removed top-level `Command`→`types.Command`) resolves as feature-additions ∪ migration-removal. Rebase onto the LATEST main right before pushing — it keeps moving; push `HEAD:main` with an `is-ancestor` fast-forward guard.

**Freshly-published versions lag on the uv index CDN.** Right after a `v*` tag publishes and the wheel is confirmed on the PyPI JSON API, `uv lock` in a downstream repo may still see only the PRIOR version ("only capt-hook<=6.5.0 available … unsatisfiable"). It's a Fastly CDN propagation lag on the simple-index edge uv reads (~6 min for capt-hook 7.0.0). `--refresh-package <name>` busts it once propagated; a fresh `uv cache clean <name>` helps; avoid bare `uv lock --refresh` (re-fetches everything, times out). So sequence family releases with a gap and re-lock downstreams last.

**ccxbench (cc-context/bench) test harness:** `uv run pytest` fails with "No module named spawnllm" because pytest isn't a declared dep, so uv runs it OUTSIDE the project env. Use `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest`. cc-context itself is a Go/Homebrew package (`ccx`); `bench` is an internal Python benchmark with no PyPI release — wave-2 there is just dep-bump + re-lock + push to main.

**GitHub Pages deploy flakes:** cc-transcript + captain-hook both hit `publish-docs → Deploy to GitHub Pages: "Deployment failed, try again later" (error_count: 10)` while `build-docs` stayed green — a transient GitHub-side infra issue, re-runnable, NOT a docs-build problem and NOT release-blocking (PyPI release is a separate workflow). Related: [[docs-build-sidebar-cost]], [[cc-transcript-build-env]].
